summary: The paragraph is faithful in most clauses, but it leaves the rulings for הרא"ש and ר"ת unapplied, makes the destroyers rather than the pillars (Job 9:6) the subject of יתפלצון, drops מראות (Isa 44:18), renders והדבר אין בהם (Jer 5:13) as 'substance', and reads אין ספק בידם as an affirmation against its context (read סיפק). Many allusions were missing from apparatus (Job 28, Esth 4:11, Josh 1:18, Gen 19:11, Ps 106:36, 107:30, 73:28, and others) and three citations were misquoted. כבשונו, מחצצים and עמם are open questions for the owner.

patches.value: 13) We learned from the words of the Gaon that there are many books that are ascribed to the names of the great sages of Israel (falsely), for the sake of some benefit that accrues to them, and we learned also that whatever is not stated explicitly in the Mishnah and in the Gemara, and that we see is the opposite of the plain sense of the Talmud, is not a tradition, and we do not rely on it. And for this reason no decisors rule from the midrashim where they disagree with the Talmud, and even the Jerusalem Talmud we do not heed where it disagrees with the Babylonian, on which all the house of Israel rely, both for leniency and for stringency, as all this is made clear in the words of our rabbis the decisors in several places. And see below, §42, what I wrote there in the name of the Rosh, and go and learn from what Rabbeinu Tam ben Yichya wrote, cited in the book Rivid ha-Zahav in the laws of Passover, and these are his words: "In our time knowledge has ceased, and the hidden matters of the Torah have been hidden from the eyes of every living thing; no man knows the order of this wisdom; and whoever holds to this, there befalls him a great share of the harm and the danger (that is to say, the harm and the danger of heresy, in that there is no share for him in the God of Israel). And concerning such things our Rabbis of blessed memory warned us, 'Do not seek what is too wondrous for you, and do not inquire into what is hidden from you.' And it is enough for us what the sages of the true tradition, agreed upon from every side, have taught us in the explanation of the Torah and its commandments. According to the tradition, from man to man, until the days of Moses; and it is called the Oral Torah, on account of which Moses went up on high and stood there forty days to learn its general principles and its particulars by the rules transmitted to him from the mouth of the Power. And with these matters we are bound to occupy ourselves, for they are our life and the length of our days, and in not one of them shall we err. His one law is to put to death whoever defies their word, and whoever transgresses the words of the Sages is liable to death. But the remaining allusions in them, which the sages of Kabbalah did not exhaust in their lifetimes, although they are hidden matters of the Torah and matters of the intellect; we were not commanded concerning them. For these remained for the select few to be occupied with them, in the times that were before us, etc. And not everyone who wishes to take the Name takes it. For these are matters that are like its furnace; they are so forever. And in our time the merit of the fathers has ended, and no one holds this wisdom justly: on the contrary, they destroy the corners of the Torah, and its pillars shudder at the sound of the trumpeters; the blind, who pass over, do not know the way where light dwells; they grope like the blind, and weary themselves seeking the door. And where they thought to gain, suddenly they shall be broken, and there is no healing. And many of the unlearned boast, saying: 'The secret of the LORD is ours; the upper waters are our heritage, not yours, you masters of the Talmud who walk in darkness.' Their heart is not with their people; their eyes are plastered over, so that they cannot see, and the word is not in them; they are wise to do harm to themselves. For they hold fast to what the hand of their intellect is too short to reach. And they want to climb the rungs; it is not in their power to reach the goal. And they bring up a potsherd in their hands to scrape with it. And they become a snare to them, etc. For there comes out from them a stumbling-block, to breach the fence of the Torah and to tear down its walls. One boasts of what he does not understand, and errs in the beginnings of the Torah and its roots, and comes to heresy. And he is distanced from the haven of his desire, which is the nearness of God; it would have been better for him had he not been created, all the more so to change a midrash and to annul a halakhah." Thus far his words.
patches.reason: Decisions: הרא"ש is 'the Rosh' and ר"ת is 'Rabbeinu Tam'. The Hebrew has a comma before וצא, so 'And go' is lower-case 'and go'. ועמודיה יתפלצון is Job 9:6, so the pillars are the subject of 'shudder'. טח מראות is Isa 44:18, 'plastered over from seeing', and מראות was left out. והדבר אין בהם is Jer 5:13, 'the word is not in them', not 'substance'. אין ספק בידם להגיע is read as אין סיפק בידם, 'it is not in their power', since the sense of the context requires it (decisions: a word that does not fit its context). Smaller: 'in not one of them shall we err' (the old order made 'err' transitive); 'take the Name' (no 'up' in the Hebrew); 'haven' for מחוז (Ps 107:30).

patches.value: Paragraph 13 of the book's third chapter. The opening 'we learned' frame is the author's; the central quotation is Rabbeinu Tam's, and it closes with the author's 'Thus far his words'.
patches.reason: Rabbeinu Tam, by the ruling.

value: The paragraph is the author's own argument in its first half. From וז"ל (3:13.102) to עכ"ל (3:13.393) the words are Rabbeinu Tam's, as cited in Rivid ha-Zahav, and the quotation is marked in double quotation marks.
ולא סמכינן עליה (3:13.37-39): סמכינן is the Talmudic Aramaic first-person plural of 'to rely', and the English gives it as the plain 'we do not rely on it'.

ועמודיה יתפלצון (3:13.280-281) is Job 9:6, where the pillars shudder. The pillars of the Torah are therefore the subject of יתפלצון, and the destroyers have only 'the corners of the Torah' as their object. The pillars shudder at the sound of the מחצצים (Judg 5:11, a word of disputed sense).
The speech of the unlearned (3:13.307-320) has no introductory formula beyond באמרם. It is marked as direct speech inside the quotation, in single quotation marks.

אין ספק בידם להגיע (3:13.342-345): the printed ספק is 'doubt', but after קצרה יד שכלם (the hand of their intellect is too short) and before the potsherd (3:13.349-352) the clause must say that they lack the means to arrive. The word is read as סיפק, 'capacity, means' (the rabbinic idiom אין סיפק בידו, 'it is not in his power'), and the English follows the sense of the context. The plain reading of ספק as 'doubt' is in readings.
patches.reason: The note on the subject of יתפלצון is now settled by Job 9:6, the note on אין ספק is changed, and Rabbi Tam becomes Rabbeinu Tam.

value: Base text: Wikisource, as translated for the unit under Q2 (the 1931 scan is not yet collated for this paragraph).
ר"ת (3:13.93): 'Rabbeinu Tam' by the editor's ruling; 'Rabbi Tam' (ר' תם) is the other expansion.
Job 28:21: ונעלמה מעיני כל חי; the author writes נעלמו מעיני כל חי (3:13.109-112). Job 28:13: לא ידע אנוש ערכה; echoed in לא ידע אנוש סדר (3:13.113-116).
Cf. Josh 22:25: ואין לכם חלק בה'; echoed in שאין לו חלק באלהי ישראל (3:13.132-136).
Deut 30:20: כי הוא חייך ואורך ימיך; the author writes כי הם חיינו ואורך ימינו (3:13.198-202).
Esth 4:11: אחת דתו להמית (3:13.207-209). Josh 1:18: כל איש אשר ימרה את פיך; the author writes אשר ימרה את פיהם (3:13.210-213).
Job 9:6: ועמודיה יתפלצון (3:13.280-281). Judg 5:11: מקול מחצצים בין משאבים (3:13.282-283).
Job 38:19: אי זה הדרך ישכן אור; the author writes דרך ישכן אור.
Isa 59:10: נגששה כעורים קיר, and Deut 28:29: כאשר ימשש העור באפלה; the author writes ימששו כעורים (3:13.291-292).
Gen 19:11: וילאו למצא הפתח (3:13.293-295).
Prov 6:15: פתע ישבר ואין מרפא; the author writes פתע ישברו ואין מרפא.
Ps 25:14: סוד ה' ליראיו; the author writes סוד ה' לנו. Deut 33:4: מורשה קהלת יעקב; the author writes מורשה לנו (3:13.311-312). Cf. Isa 9:1: ההלכים בחשך (3:13.319-320).
Isa 44:18: טח מראות עיניהם (מראות, 'from seeing'; the verse governs the sense of 3:13.324-326).
Jer 5:13: והדבר אין בהם (3:13.327-329). Jer 4:22: חכמים המה להרע; echoed in חכמים להרע לנפשם (3:13.330-332).
Isa 59:1: הן לא קצרה יד ה' מהושיע; cf. Num 11:23: היד ה' תקצר; echoed in קצרה יד שכלם (3:13.336-338).
אין ספק (3:13.342-343): printed ספק 'doubt'; the likelier word is סיפק 'capacity, means' (decisions, wave 1: a word that does not fit its context).
Job 2:8: ויקח לו חרש להתגרד בו; echoed in חרס בידם להתגרד בו (3:13.349-351).
Ps 106:36: ויהיו להם למוקש, cut short by the author with וכו' (3:13.353-356). Cf. Eccl 10:8: ופרץ גדר (3:13.361-362).
patches.reason: Allusions not listed: Job 28:21 and 28:13, Esth 4:11, Josh 1:18, Deut 30:20, Job 9:6, Judg 5:11, Gen 19:11 (וילאו למצא הפתח), Deut 33:4, Isa 9:1, Jer 5:13, Ps 106:36, Ps 107:30, Ps 73:28. Misquoted: Isa 59:10 has נגששה כעורים קיר (ימששו is Deut 28:29, Job 12:25); Isa 59:1 begins הן; Prov 6:15 reads פתע ישבר. The ר"ת line follows the ruling.

ספק as printed is 'doubt', but the clause needs סיפק, 'capacity, means' (אין סיפק בידו, 'it is not in his power'). After קצרה יד שכלם and before 'a potsherd in their hands' an affirmative 'no doubt that it is in their power' contradicts the argument.

patches.value: The printed word is ספק, 'doubt'. The context needs סיפק, 'capacity, means', as in the rabbinic אין סיפק בידו, 'it is not in his power'. Translated by the sense of the context, with the printed word here and in apparatus (decisions, wave 1). The plain reading is in readings.

patches.value: להגיע depends on סיפק: 'capacity to reach'.
patches.reason: The old note said the clause is affirmative; it is not.

patches.value: כבשונו שלעולם: probably the rabbinic idiom כבשונו של עולם ('the furnace of the world'), meaning the Creator's inscrutable secret; the printed text joins של and עולם. The English keeps 'like its furnace' until the owner rules.
patches.reason: Decisions are silent. The translator's 'like its furnace; they are so forever' leaves 'its' with no antecedent and takes שלעולם as 'forever'. Proposed ruling: read כבשונו של עולם as one idiom and translate 'the furnace of the world', with the meaning in a note. If accepted, the clause becomes: For these are matters that are the furnace of the world, they are. (the second הם is emphatic; the owner may prefer to drop it). The translator's version is kept as the main text until the owner rules.

patches.value: מחצצים is the word of Judg 5:11 (מקול מחצצים בין משאבים), where its sense is disputed ('archers', 'dividers of spoil', 'musicians'). 'Trumpeters' would be מחצצרים, a different word. The English keeps 'trumpeters' until the owner rules.
patches.reason: Decisions are silent. The old note derives the word from blowing a trumpet, but the Hebrew has no ר and the phrase is Judg 5:11. Proposed ruling: render 'the sound of the archers' (Judg 5:11), with the other senses in a note, or transliterate the word. The translator's version stays until the owner rules.

patches.value: עמם is עִמָּם, 'with them' (their heart is not with them: they have no sense), or עַמָּם, 'their people'. The English has 'their people'.
patches.reason: Decisions are silent. 'Their heart is not with their people' makes no point beside 'there is no word in them' and 'they are wise to do harm'. Proposed ruling: 'Their heart is not with them' (they have no sense). The translator's version stays until the owner rules.

value.english: there is no doubt that it is in their power to reach the goal
value.note: The translator's first reading. It makes the clause an affirmation, against קצרה יד שכלם before it and the potsherd after it, so the main English reads סיפק, 'capacity'.

value.note: The printed שלעולם is read as של עולם; the main English keeps the translator's 'like its furnace'.
